title: Building a Claude API Literature Screening Pipeline for an Asian American Breast Cancer Review
goal: Develop and debug a Python script that uses the Claude API to analyze PubMed-exported article data and assist with literature screening by generating structured include, exclude, or maybe recommendations based on predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria.
context: This task builds on the literature review workflow from Session 1. Because screening a large number of PubMed records can be time-consuming, the goal is to develop a Python-based tool that uses the Claude API to assist with title and abstract screening. The script will read PubMed-exported article information, apply the review’s inclusion and exclusion criteria, and generate a structured screening recommendation and rationale for each paper.
occupation: Phd student in family social science.

session_goal_achievement.Why or why not: I achieved my goal of developing the script. But the script was not tested on the whole sample data yet because we decided to add another manual checking section.

Step 1+2+3.step_name: Inspect and prepare the exported literature meta data + Design the Claude API screening prompt and output format + Implement the Claude API call in Python
Step 1+2+3.step_action: Create a prompt that provides Claude with the literature review question, inclusion criteria, exclusion criteria, and the title and abstract of one article. Define a structured response format that requires the model to return a screening recommendation, a brief rationale, and any uncertainty or missing information relevant to the decision.

nodes.label: Frame the holistic task to Claude Code
nodes.detail: In a new 'Article screening workflow planning' session (project folder title_abstract, containing articles.bib and Inclusion criteria.docx), the participant types and sends a single prompt asking Claude to restructure the bib file, write the Python analysis code, and prepare the prompts, explicitly requesting plan mode only ('don't change anything yet, ask me if anything is unclear').

nodes.label: Inspect project files and report data-quality findings
nodes.detail: Claude inspects articles.bib and Inclusion criteria.docx to understand the literature data and screening criteria. It reports the 735-entry BibTeX structure and identifies data-quality issues, including corrupted language/publication-type fields in 53 PsycInfo records, polluted author fields, and 9 non-English records, before asking for clarification on a few screening decisions.

nodes.label: Check the criteria Google Doc
Retry Claude in the intended directory
nodes.detail: The user notices Claude is still working in the wrong directory, stops the generation, and prompts Claude again after navigating to AsianAW/title_abstract.

nodes.label: Build and verify the literature-screening pipeline
nodes.detail: Claude reports that the pipeline is built and verifies the restructuring, response handling, export, and scoring components using the 735 records and synthetic responses. It also identifies two implementation fixes, confirms 9 records are auto-excluded and 726 remain for screening, and notes that API-based screening is still untested because credentials are unavailable.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about exploring project files and understanding the literature data
Request per-criterion structured output
nodes.detail: The participant rejects the initial single-decision output format and types a revision request: 'change the structured output to include the evaluation of each criteria (4 in total)'.

nodes.label: Update plan with per-criterion verdicts and aggregation rule
nodes.detail: Claude updates the plan so each record's output carries a PASS/UNCLEAR/FAIL verdict for population, topic, content, and publication type, plus an aggregation rule (all four PASS -> INCLUDE, any FAIL -> EXCLUDE, otherwise MAYBE) mapped 1:1 onto the docx's criteria.

nodes.label: Review Claude's responses on the screening plan and restructuring implementation
nodes.detail: The user reviews Claude's responses about updating the screening plan with per-criterion verdicts and an aggregation rule, as well as implementing and self-correcting the restructuring script.

nodes.label: Switch to Auto mode and approve the plan
nodes.detail: The participant opens the permission-mode selector, chooses Auto mode (Claude handles permission decisions), and approves the plan, after which Claude begins implementation by writing screening/prepare_records.py.

nodes.label: Implement, verify, and hand off the screening pipeline
nodes.detail: Claude runs prepare_records.py, catches and fixes two bugs mid-implementation (a record missing a language field was wrongly auto-excluded; PsycInfo DOI URLs needed normalization), then verifies parse round-trips. With no API credentials on the machine, Claude writes screening/screen.py (Batch API, adaptive thinking, full CLI flags), build_gold_sample.py, and export_results.py, testing all end-to-end against synthetic stubs before removing the test artifacts. Claude then reports the pipeline is structurally verified, explicitly declines to handle the API key ("You'll need to set the key yourself — I won't handle it"), and hands off an ordered checklist: export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY → install dependencies → check cost estimate → run a 5-record smoke test → label the gold sample.

nodes.label: Navigate Finder to records.csv
Inspect the restructured records table
nodes.detail: The participant opens the generated records.csv in Numbers, which imports as a 727-row table with columns including authors, language, and pub_type, and reviews it to verify the restructured literature metadata looks correct.

nodes.label: Request abstract-less records be routed to MAYBE
nodes.detail: The participant types a refinement instruction: 'for articles without abstract, mark them as MAYBE, and do not pipe to API'.

nodes.label: Reroute title-only records to a deterministic rule
nodes.detail: Claude updates prompts.py and screen.py so the 16 title-only records (and the 9 non-English records) are decided by a local rule rather than sent to the API, regenerates the affected output files (rule_decisions.csv, records split by route), and re-verifies the counts reconcile to 735.

nodes.label: Review rule decisions and determine next actions
nodes.detail: The participant inspects rule_decisions.csv, reviews Claude's response about rerouting title-only records to a deterministic rule, and asks Claude for a clear list of next actions to proceed.

nodes.label: Provide numbered checklist and explain API key setup
nodes.detail: Claude gives a numbered action list (set API key, install dependencies, check cost, smoke test, label the gold set) and, as the participant asks where to paste her key, explains the difference between a session-only export and a persistent ~/.zshrc entry.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about the numbered checklist and API key setup

Review Claude's response about where to put the command
Follow the instruction code steps
Report missing requirements file error
nodes.detail: Prompts: 'in step two i encountered ERROR: Could not open requirements file: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'screening/requirements.txt''.

nodes.label: Provide steps to resolve the directory error
Skim Claude's steps to resolve the directory error
Hit a python-not-found error in Terminal
nodes.detail: The participant runs the estimate command in Terminal and gets 'zsh: command not found: python'; Claude diagnoses that macOS ships python3 not python and revises every command in the checklist accordingly.

nodes.label: Provide corrected Python commands for the screening steps
Run and report the cost estimate
nodes.detail: The participant reruns python3 screening/screen.py --estimate in Terminal, successfully obtains a projected batch cost of $6.57, and copies the estimate to Claude for review.

nodes.label: Revise the cost estimate against real token usage
nodes.detail: Claude checks the actual token usage from the smoke test against its assumption and finds real output is 129 tokens/record rather than the conservative 500 assumed, revising the projected full-batch cost down to about $3.28.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about revising the cost estimate against real token usage
Revisit Claude's response about the list of actions to do
Run the 5-record smoke test
nodes.detail: The participant runs 'python3 screening/screen.py --limit 5 --sync', making the first real Claude API calls of the session; five plausible screening decisions come back, e.g. excluding a general-population national statistics report and including several on-topic Asian American breast-screening studies.

nodes.label: Copy paste the results of the 5-record smoke test
Review smoke-test results and recommend next steps
Review Claude's response about the recommended next steps
Build the stratified gold sample and open the gold_sample_template.csv for review
nodes.detail: The participant runs 'python3 screening/build_gold_sample.py' in Terminal, which computes stratum pool sizes (AANHPI-specific, general-population, disease-burden, random) and draws a stratified 50-record sample into data/gold/gold_sample_template.csv with an empty human_decision column. The participant opens the newly generated gold_sample_template.csv in Numbers, which imports as a 51-row by 10-column table, beginning the transition into manual gold-sample review.

Step 5.step_name: Design the gold sample that helps tune the model performance
Step 5.step_action: Design a stratified sample of 50 articles for the researcher to manually screen and give feedback to check against the model decision, to improve the model accuracy.

nodes.label: Begin manual review of gold-sample abstracts
nodes.detail: The participant starts reading through the gold sample row by row, clicking into individual abstract cells (breast cancer subtype risk studies, South Asian immigrant screening focus groups, correction notices) to judge each record from title and abstract alone, as instructed, rather than consulting full text.

nodes.label: Continue reading abstracts and cross-check labeling instructions
nodes.detail: The participant continues clicking through further abstracts (national disparities estimates, mammographic bone-density studies, limited-English-proficiency access barriers).

nodes.label: Read further gold-sample records
nodes.detail: The participant continues the row-by-row abstract review, reading additional records including a church-based 'Faith in Action' breast-screening intervention trial among Korean American women and a Korean-language media content-analysis study.

nodes.label: Cross-check bibliographic metadata while labeling
nodes.detail: The participant scrolls to view the year, journal, pub_type, and keywords columns alongside the abstract column for individual records, cross-referencing bibliographic details as part of the manual labeling pass.

nodes.label: Continue reading remaining abstracts
nodes.detail: The participant continues reading further records, including a multiethnic mammography self-report validation study and a Pakistani clinic parity/breastfeeding-and-breast-density study, still working through the 50-row sample.

nodes.label: Recording ends with labeling still in progress
nodes.detail: The recording ends with the participant still reading gold-sample abstracts in Numbers; the human_decision column had not visibly been filled in for the sampled frames, consistent with the manual ~1 hour of gold-sample labeling being unfinished at the end of the session.
